text: Useful bits in a matrix, and for each row, it computes a parity bit, and for each column, also it computes a parity bit. So we increase the number of parity bits. So we make our code more powerful, right? And this is indeed true, because if you notice, in this case, where in this example, where we consider that the receiver makes one mistake, it will be able not just to detect that it has made a mistake, but it will also be able to correct the mistake. So in making the code more powerful, because we now increase the number of redundant bits, so we reduce the coding rate, we are able not just to perform detection of a single error, but also to correct a single error. And again, you can do that as a small exercise, atom, and verify that this is indeed true. Remember that the waiting's work is that the receiver will try first to modulate the information bits, the user bits with a white background, and then compute locally the parity bits based on what it has expected, and then compare the parity bits that it has computed locally with the parity bits that it has received from the transmitter, and use this to understand.
